description: Reference choreography from the @deatonioo TikTok (trio in a parking garage; the reference dancer is the creator in the middle, white tee and grey pants, tracker id 2; 6.5 s clip, all of it dance). Move boundaries from the wrist trajectories (mean wrist x/y relative to the hip centre), hip-over-ankle shift, shoulder width (body turns) and arm motion energy of data/dance/pose/deatonioo_200136.npz, checked against frame strips of data/dance/raw/deatonioo_200136.mp4 and data/dance/pose/deatonioo_200136.pose.mp4 (see docs/DANCE_MODEL_INTERFACE.md section 4 for the schema). Sides are given as seen on screen; the learner mirrors the screen.
bpm_estimate_note: Estimated, not from a track id: onset autocorrelation of the clip audio peaks at 0.998 s (60 bpm, a kick every two beats) and 0.499 s (120.2 bpm); the strong sub-150 Hz kicks sit at 0.21, 1.21, 2.21, 3.20, 4.21, 4.70, 5.21, 6.21 s (about 119.96 bpm) and a 120 bpm grid at phase 0.205 s collects 2.7x the mean low-band onset strength (1.2x at the 0.46 s phase, which is the off-beat clap/hat that the full-band estimate of 0.43 s locked onto). The dancer's hand sweeps land on that grid (hands come to rest at 1.25, 2.23, 3.20, 4.17, 4.70, 5.23 s): slow sweeps every two beats, then two one-beat sweeps, then the arms-up hit, so 120 bpm, not 60 (an 8-count of 8 s would not fit the clip). Treat as 120 +/- 1 bpm, beat grid 0.21 + 0.5k s.

moves.name: Ready: walks backward from the camera into place, hands loose at the sides

Slow sweeps at stomach height, both hands swinging together to the screen-left, across to the screen-right and back to the screen-left, each held for two beats; the body turns toward the hands while the hips push the other way
Quick double sweep, hands snap across to the screen-right and straight back to the screen-left, one beat each

Both arms shoot up overhead, screen-left arm reaching up and out, screen-right elbow bent out with the hand over the head, held for two beats leaning a little to the screen-left, then starting to come down

notes: The clip is 195 frames (6.5 s, already trimmed before the TikTok end card); the creator is tracked (ok=True) in 194 of them and the final move ends at the last frame (194, t=6.466 s).

Tracker id 2 is the creator in the middle (white tee, grey pants), on him for the whole clip including the close-up walk-back at 0-1 s. The other long tracks (id 1, 195 frames; id 6, 173 frames; both with low overlap with id 2) are the two side dancers, who are partly cut off at the frame edges and do arm variations, so they were not used.
'ready' is the walk-in: the dancer starts close to the camera and backs into place until about 1.0 s; the first sweep lands on the beat at 1.21 s.

Beat grid 0.21 + 0.5k s at 120 bpm. Lesson part (first_beat_s = count_in_s = 2.21, one full 8-count 2.21-6.21 s): count 1 hands land at the screen-right, 3 sweep back to the screen-left, 5 snap right, 6 snap left, the arms fly up on the and-of-6 and land on 7 (5.21 s), held through 8. This is the last full 8-count that fits (2.71 + 4.0 s would run past 6.466 s) and the only one that contains the arms-up hit and its hold, the trio's signature pose; 1.21-5.21 s (the phrase-aligned 8 counts of sweeps) would end exactly as the arms arrive overhead.

Sweeps: the hands swing during the off-beat and come to rest on the beat (rest at 1.25, 2.23, 3.20 s every two beats, then 4.17 and 4.70 s one beat apart). Shoulder width drops to about 0.5 torso lengths when the hands are at the screen-left (body turned toward them) and the hips shift about 0.15 torso lengths the opposite way over the feet.

Feet stay planted shoulder-width apart for the whole dance (ankle separation steady at 0.65-0.8 torso lengths after the walk-in); ankles are visible (mean keypoint confidence 0.87), so leg faults can fire, but there is no footwork to teach.
Screen-left/right in move names are image sides of the clip; with learner_mirrors_screen the learner's own right hand follows the screen-right side.
